long_biography.plain_text:
U2 began with a notice Larry Mullen Jr. pinned to a Dublin school bulletin board in 1976. David Evans answered it as a teenage guitarist, joining the group that passed through the names Feedback and The Hype before becoming U2. He adopted The Edge as his stage name and developed a rhythmic, effects-shaped guitar vocabulary that became central to the band's sound.

His contribution extended beyond lead guitar to keyboards, backing vocals and shared songwriting, roles that helped make recording and touring the foundations of his career. U2's 2005 Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction and Evans's Grammy record mark that collective achievement. He has also taken on production work: for Songs of Surrender, he curated and produced newly recorded interpretations of the band's earlier material, treating the catalogue as continuing creative work.
